regime_context: The detector shows a two-tier precious-metals leadership (Gold Miners, then Silver & Royalties) atop a broad eligible set (8 of 16), with the absolute-trend gate validating as risk control (gate_helps true) and cross-sectional momentum flagged as attention-only. No one-narrative regime is dominant, and the macro backdrop is 92% unscheduled-news driven, so I treat the thematic hierarchy as a coincident focus lens and keep leans conditional and modest.
emerging_watch: Watch whether Silver & Royalties closes the 0.147 rotation margin over Gold Miners to below 0.05 AND improves its durability_bar above Gold's; if both happen for three consecutive sessions, it would suggest a leadership handoff within the precious-metals complex rather than a mere cohesive rally. If instead Gold's durability_bar re-widens above 0.10, the watch retires.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners hold the #1 rank, are trend-gate eligible, show full breadth (1.0) and the highest durability bar (0.73) with a mixed Hurst tag — suggesting leadership is intact but not in a clean trend. The ONE validated leg here is the absolute-trend gate, which supports staying on the right side of the incumbent leader rather than forecasting outperformance. Given rank-IC near zero, direction is inferred from trend-health, not from the score itself.
evidence: gate_helps=true supports trend-discipline as risk control
theses.dissent: The rank is an attention lens with nearly zero predictive IC; mixed Hurst means the trend lacks the staying-power signature of a clean uptrend; the macro desk is dominated by geopolitics with 92% unscheduled headline flow, so a single news shock can unwind precious-metals leadership quickly.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes below its own 20-day average and Gold Miners' durability_bar drops under 0.50 before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties sit immediately behind the gold leader (rank 2) with full breadth and a mean-revert Hurst tag, which tempers the trend read. The rotation margin to Gold (0.147) is tight enough to suggest a cohesive precious-metals complex rather than a handoff. The honest basis for a lean is the eligible trend gate plus cohesion, not predicted outperformance.
evidence: rotation.margin=0.147 to leader across same category
theses.dissent: Mean-revert Hurst directly argues against extrapolating strength; silver's volatility is higher than gold's; ETF proxy is shared (XGD.TO with Gold Miners) so the two are practically the same position, inflating apparent diversification.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO underperforms Gold Miners by 3% over 10 trading days and Silver & Royalties' durability_bar falls below 0.45.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas Producers rank 3 and are trend-eligible, but carry the crowding flag (crowded=true, crowding_z=1.2) and weaker breadth (0.714). The guardrails forbid treating crowding as a sell or short, and forbid fading the leader — but this is a rank-3 theme with a crowding caution, so the disciplined read is to avoid fresh exposure rather than chase it. The trend gate is the only validated edge and it does not argue for adding to an already-crowded name.
evidence: guardrails: crowding is a size-down caution, never a short
theses.dissent: Energy has a durable macro tailwind (energy is a top macro-narrative theme) and the trend gate still says eligible, so an avoid lean may under-participate in a rotation toward a still-leading cyclical.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO makes a new 21-day high and Oil & Gas Producers' breadth rises above 0.90 with no further crowding escalation before the check-by date.

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
